audit.report: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 337615) sat idle in transaction for 4.1 seconds and became the root blocker for 12 waiting sessions, collapsing checkout success from 90% to 0% over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian accepted after trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$274,743 (896s remaining runtime) versus a 4-minute replay cost for the interruptible batch job. Authority authorized the termination in round 1, the executor killed the session, and the verifier confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits, 100% checkout success over 10 seconds, and no protected settlements affected. Total negotiation and recovery duration was 57.8 seconds, well within the 60-second business tolerance.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 337615) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4.1s, blocking checkout sessions and driving success rate to 0%.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_inventory to auto-abort idle transactions before they become multi-second blockers.
Pre-register the 4-minute replay cost and may_interrupt policy for inventory_reconcile in the workload registry so trade-off calculations are instant and require no live probes.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians acted on complete evidence in a single round: the Database Guardian cited lock waits, SLO breach, revenue impact, workload replayability, and a prior verified memory; the Continuity Guardian validated the cost asymmetry (~$274k wait vs 4-min replay) and accepted without objection. No round was wasted and no invariant overrode the decision.
follow_ups: Implement idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 2s for the batch_worker role to prevent recurrence.
Add batch_replayable_inventory to the change calendar as a pre-approved interruptible workload for future incidents.
Review why the batch job entered idle-in-transaction state (application logic or pool configuration) and fix the root cause.
